newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on pork export ban.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on pork export ban.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished sharply lower on Friday as an export ban on fresh and frozen pork and the government's latest attempt to cool down the overheated market triggered heavy selling, brokers said.
The weighted index plunged 262.60 points or 3.09 percent to 8,230.07. Turnover was a frantic T$189.67 billion.
Food shares tumbled 5.90 percent after the government on Thursday announced export ban on fresh and frozen pork due to an outbreak of the contagious foot and mouth disease.

Also further dampening confidence was a letter written by the Securities and Exchange Commission chief Lu Tung-ying to the island's securities brokerages, urging them to protect investors' rights after recent market rallies.
The letter was widely seen by analysts as an attempt to cool down the overheated market.
"The hog foot-and-mouth disease had a huge impact on related food and livestock companies," Tsao Chung-ping, an analyst for Ting Kong Securities, said.
"The SEC letter is quite discouraging as well," Tsao said.

The central bank's recent non-stop issuance of negotiable certificates of deposits was widely seen in the market as aimed at keeping a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the stock market's rally.
The bank said on Friday it was issuing T$3 billion in one-month NCDs later in the day.
"All this negative news will force the market to enter a correction phase," Tsao said.
Most livestock shares plunged by the daily seven percent limit, with Hui Shung Agriculture losing T$2 to T$26.6.
Textiles and electronics were also weak.
Recent gainer, United Microelectronics, was down T$3 or 5.77 percent to T$49.
Brokers said they expected the market to consolidate next week, with initial support seen at 8,000 points.
